lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Morning, both of you. Okay, I've got the Ducal call at ten thirty, so let's keep this tight. Tybalt, you want to start?

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Sure. So, good news. The Android 11 crash is fixed.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Wait, really? Already?

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Yeah. It was the photo cache. On older Android we were writing thumbnails to a cache path that, um, the system can clear out from under us. So the app goes to read a photo it just took, the file's gone, and it falls over.

lines.speaker: nurse_angela
lines.text: Huh. So it wasn't the camera at all.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Nope. Camera's fine. I moved the cache into app storage and added a check so a missing thumbnail just gets regenerated instead of crashing. Both of the crash reports reproduce on my test phone before the fix, and neither one does after.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: That's great. Thank you. Is it in the beta build yet?

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: It'll be in tonight's build. I'll ping the two testers who reported it and ask them to update.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Perfect. Angela, where are we on the checklist?

lines.speaker: nurse_angela
lines.text: So the release checklist is about eighty percent done. Store listing, screenshots, the release notes you wrote yesterday, the rollback plan, all of that's checked off.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: And the other twenty?

lines.speaker: nurse_angela
lines.text: Mostly QA. I need a sign-off from Balthasar, and he won't give it until he's rerun the offline-sync tests with his fix in. Which, honestly, is the right call.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Agreed. Do you think we'll have that before Friday?

lines.speaker: nurse_angela
lines.text: I think so. I'm going to grab him tomorrow afternoon and go through it together. If anything's shaky, I'll tell you before the go or no-go, not during it.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Thank you. Friday nine thirty still works for everyone?

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Works for me.

lines.speaker: nurse_angela
lines.text: It's on the calendar.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Okay. One more thing from me. Tybalt, your worry from Monday, about Schema Bridge depending on Mesh Routing being up?

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Still worried, yeah.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: So I brought it up with Romeo in the kickoff, and he's building a local queue on our side. If Mesh Routing goes down, Balcony just keeps working. Inspections pile up in the queue on the device and send when the service is back. Nobody in the field even notices.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Okay. That's, um, that's actually the right answer.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Don't sound so surprised.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: I'm not. Okay, a little. Look, if it survives a week of airplane mode, I'm satisfied.

lines.speaker: nurse_angela
lines.text: Can I write that down? Tybalt, satisfied.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Conditionally satisfied. Write the condition down too.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Fair. I'm meeting with Romeo at three, he's supposed to show me the prototype. I'll tell you how it holds up.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Sounds good.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Okay, that's it. Thanks, both of you. Go do good things.
